secretHandling.transitMethod: The Access Key ID and Secret Access Key were moved from the Cloudflare console into the file via the system clipboard — the console's own copy control, then a shell read. The values were never rendered into a tool result, a screenshot, a log or a chat message. Only their lengths and shapes (32-hex and 64-hex) were ever observed.
secretHandling.mode600EnforcementProven: The wrapper was run against a deliberately chmod-644 file and REFUSED it: 'has mode 644; it must be 600. Refusing to read it.' Exit 78.
secretHandling.quotingDefectFound: The first scheduled run failed with 'BACKUP_SOURCE_DATABASE_URL is not set' while the value sat plainly in the file. Cause: the file is SOURCED by bash and a connection string contains '&', which bash reads as background-the-command. All values are now single-quoted and backup.env.example documents the requirement.

scheduler.hostCategory: product owner's MacBook Pro (Apple Silicon), single logged-in user
scheduler.scheduleBasis: Chosen from measurement: the 02:00-07:00 band showed wake activity on 6-7 of 8 days, the most consistent coverage of any hour.

tccFinding.what: macOS TCC denies a launchd user agent access to ~/Desktop, ~/Documents and ~/Downloads.
tccFinding.howFound: The first scheduled run exited 126 'Operation not permitted'. A diagnostic launchd agent then established it precisely: the repository script could be stat-ed but NOT read, and ~/Desktop could not be listed at all. File permissions are irrelevant.
tccFinding.rejectedAlternative: Granting Full Disk Access to /bin/bash would hand every script the user ever runs the keys to the whole filesystem in order to fix one backup job.
tccFinding.consequence: The installer copies the four job files plus one dependency into ~/.safety-insite/runner/, records per-file sha256 in INSTALLED.json, and --verify reports drift against the checkout.

scheduler.npmRootFinding: The runner needs its own package.json: without one npm walks up, finds an unrelated package.json in the home directory, and fails on ITS peer dependencies (an Expo conflict, in a backup installer).
scheduler.sourceBindingFinding: The runner is not a git checkout, so the first durable artifact recorded applicationSourceDigest as unbound. The installer now computes the digest from the checkout at install time and writes SOURCE-BINDING.json; artifacts report status RECORDED_AT_INSTALL rather than COMPUTED, so the provenance is never overstated.
scheduler.installationProof: launchctl print reports the agent loaded with Hour=5 Minute=0; runs=3; last exit code = 0 after the successful run.

rpoResidualRisk.measured: 644 wake events over the power log's full 8-day retention; longest continuous gap 16.0 hours; no day without a wake; 17 days uninterrupted uptime; reboots roughly monthly.
rpoResidualRisk.credible: On that evidence a daily job runs daily — launchd executes a missed StartCalendarInterval job at the next wake.
rpoResidualRisk.residual: An extended POWERED-OFF period violates the 24-hour RPO AND simultaneously prevents the local freshness monitor from reporting the violation, because both run on the same machine.
rpoResidualRisk.statedLimit: This is a Beta-appropriate posture, NOT an unconditional 24-hour SLA. RPO is measured from LAST SUCCESSFUL BACKUP, not from the scheduled invocation.

retentionProof.defectFixed: The §311 retention pass had a real hole: after an outage longer than the daily window, every artifact would be past the cutoff and the pass would delete the lot, emptying the destination at the moment its contents mattered most. ALWAYS_KEEP_NEWEST is an absolute floor the age rules cannot override.

st4Disposition.state: CLOSED AS AN INVESTIGATION, with an adverse finding
st4Disposition.finding: Customer evidence in insite-production is NOT recoverable after accidental delete or overwrite. R2 has no object versioning at all; no bucket lock is configured; the only lifecycle rule aborts incomplete multipart uploads; Data Access Logs are disabled. Cloudflare's eleven-nines durability explicitly 'does not prevent intentional or accidental deletion of data'.
st4Disposition.notRemediated: By product-owner instruction: no bucket lock, no lifecycle change, no Data Access Logs, no change to the customer-evidence bucket, and no copying of evidence into insite-backups/evidence/.
st4Disposition.whyBucketLockIsNotADropInFix: The product hard-deletes R2 objects in normal operation — upload rollback (storage.service.ts:145), retireReportArtifact on report regeneration (:213, called twice from canonical-reports.service.ts), and customer tombstone (:224). A lock would break report regeneration and customer erasure.

br5Disposition.databaseHalf: OPERATIONAL — dedicated destination, isolated credential proven both ways, scheduled, retention implemented and watched to fail, failure detection with four states, remote-copy restore proven, application proven on the restored data, DR runbook updated.
br5Disposition.objectHalf: UNRESOLVED — a plausible single storage mistake can permanently destroy customer evidence with no recovery mechanism. BR-5's closure rule forbids closing over that.
